If I could change one thing about iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, I would disable the new swipe-down gesture to summon Siri AI. There are already plenty of ways to invoke Siri, and I've always been used to swiping down on my iPhone and iPad to open the notification center, so this new operation doesn't affect my habit.

As for the Mac side, macOS 27 Golden Gate is almost entirely good news. Even though it's already the end of August, the new beta versions have still added many welcome changes. However, before macOS 27 officially launches next month, there's still one more change I'd like to see.

macOS 27 Golden Gate makes it harder to view the battery percentage on MacBook

macOS 27 Golden Gate has redesigned the battery controls on the menu bar. By default, it only shows the battery icon, not the percentage.

At first glance, this doesn't seem to be a problem. I've even turned off the percentage display on my iPhone myself, which uses a similar battery icon. However, I've always really liked being able to see the percentage on my Mac.

If you turn on the "Show Percentage" option in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the number is placed inside the battery icon. I assume Apple wanted to keep the design consistent with the iPhone on iOS 27.

Placing the percentage inside the iPhone battery icon was a compromise Apple made to deal with the limited space on the right side of the notch or Dynamic Island. But on Mac, even on the menu bar, I've never run into a situation where there isn't enough screen space.

I've been running macOS 27 Golden Gate on a 15-inch MacBook Air since the first developer beta. I've found that I check the battery percentage less often overall because it's harder for me to read.

I hope Apple reconsiders this point in future design decisions, especially if more users feel this design is problematic. In the meantime, I've at least found a workaround myself.

I used Codex to write a simple menu bar utility that clearly displays the battery status and percentage the way I want. If you find it useful, you can download and install it for free here.
